comment: Hand-computed worked examples for the ADR-0011 day score. The server suite alone reads this file: the iOS score mirror that once transcribed the same table was deleted 2026-10-01 (ADR-0007 mirror #4). Expected values are hand-derived from the ADR formula, never generated by the code under test.
toleranceNote: Every `expected` here is the MATHEMATICALLY EXACT value, not the IEEE754 double your implementation will produce. Compare within an epsilon of 1e-9 — never by exact equality. Worked example: two-sided-inside-high is exactly 30, but 100*(1-7/10) evaluates to 30.000000000000004 in binary floating point, so an == assertion fails on a correct implementation. The dayCases are the one exception: their `expected` is the output of an integer round-and-clamp, so those compare exactly (and `null` compares as null, not as 0).
dayCasesNote: dayCases are driven differently from the other two groups: `hourScores` are PRECOMPUTED HOUR SCORES (0..100), not metric values, and they exercise only the day-level step — mean over the array, round to nearest (HALF-UP), clamp to 1..100, or null when the array is empty. Feed them to that step directly by whatever route your code allows. One way, used by the server suite: build one stub hour per entry against an identity threshold — a two-sided band {min:0,max:200} has centre 100 and half-width 100, so its depth formula 100*(1-|v-100|/100) reduces to v for any v in 0..100, making each stub hour score exactly its `hourScores` entry. Note that hour scores are NOT rounded before the day mean, so an implementation must keep them fractional: see `plain-mean-rounds`, whose 62.5 is a genuine half-way tie.

metricCases.name: two-sided-min-edge
metricCases.derivation: |10-20|=10 -> 100*(1-10/10)=0; inside the band (inclusive) but zero depth

metricCases.name: two-sided-max-edge
metricCases.derivation: |30-20|=10 -> 100*(1-10/10)=0; inside the band (inclusive) but zero depth

metricCases.name: min-only-at-bound
metricCases.derivation: one-sided -> binary; 10 >= min 10, inclusive exactly as checkThreshold -> 100

metricCases.name: max-only-at-bound
metricCases.derivation: one-sided -> binary; 30 <= max 30, inclusive exactly as checkThreshold -> 100

metricCases.name: null-value
metricCases.derivation: absent data fails rather than passing silently (the B2 posture) -> 0

metricCases.name: degenerate-band-at-bound
metricCases.derivation: APPENDED. min===max: half-width 0, so the centre is undefined -> the ADR's one-sided ruling applies, binary; 20 inside -> 100

hourCases.name: required-miss-scores-metric-zero
hourCases.derivation: temp 35 > max 30 on a REQUIRED threshold -> 0 for temp only (the hour is NOT zeroed — amended ADR-0011, 2026-10-01); windSpeed 10 <= max 20 -> 100; mean(0,100)=50

hourCases.name: null-on-required-scores-metric-zero
hourCases.derivation: temp null fails a REQUIRED threshold (B2: absent data fails) -> 0 for temp only (the hour is NOT zeroed — amended ADR-0011, 2026-10-01); windSpeed 10 <= max 20 -> 100; mean(0,100)=50

hourCases.name: optional-miss-still-averages
hourCases.derivation: temp at centre -> 100; windSpeed 25 > max 20 (optional, no zeroing) -> 0; mean(100,0)=50

hourCases.name: display-only-metric-excluded
hourCases.derivation: only temp is thresholded; display-only humidity never contributes -> mean(100)=100

hourCases.name: null-optional-drags-mean
hourCases.derivation: temp null on an OPTIONAL threshold -> 0 but no zeroing; windSpeed 10 <= 20 -> 100; mean(0,100)=50

hourCases.name: empty-thresholds-scores-100
hourCases.derivation: APPENDED. The degenerate end of the show-but-don't-judge gap: validateActivities accepts thresholds:{} alongside a non-empty displayMetrics, so nothing at all is judged. There is no mean to take, and the tiebreaker is the verdict: evaluateHour's allPass stays true over an empty threshold map, so the hour rates "perfect" and 100 is the only score consistent with it. NOT null (null is reserved for a zero-window-hour BUCKET) and never NaN

dayCases.name: all-zero-clamps-to-1
dayCases.derivation: mean(0,0,0,0)=0 -> round 0 -> clamped up to 1 (the ring always has a drawable numeral)

dayCases.name: rounds-to-zero-clamps-to-1
dayCases.derivation: mean(1,0,0)=0.333... -> round half-up -> 0 -> clamped up to 1

dayCases.name: plain-mean-rounds
dayCases.derivation: mean(50,75)=62.5 -> round half-UP (not banker's/half-to-even, which would give 62) -> 63

dayCases.name: full-day-100
dayCases.derivation: mean(100,100,100)=100 -> 100; the upper clamp is a no-op

dayCases.name: empty-window-null
dayCases.derivation: zero window hours -> null per the ADR null rule; never 0 and never clamped to 1
